title: Transit Hub Planning Lead
statement:
**Weekly Report — Cycle 116. Elena Soria Dominguez, Transit Hub Planning Lead.**

Here's what's on the record this week, and here's what actually changed.

**Fruitvale.** The hub's visioning phase is complete and it's showing where it counts: 9,343 riders this cycle, up from 8,943 — a 4.5% gain — with the best on-time performance of any station in the system at 0.83. No BART train events on the sheet. No payments out on INIT-003 this cycle. So I want to be clear with the Mayor and the council: the numbers moved, but nothing was built. That's ridership following life, not a drawing.

**The rest of the system.** On-time performance came down citywide — 12th Street 0.86 to 0.81, 19th Street 0.81 to 0.78, Lake Merritt 0.83 to 0.77. 12th Street lost 2,313 riders and 19th Street 2,251. I told this room in an earlier cycle not to hang that on the hub, and I'll say it again, though this week I'd note it plainly: game-day crowds through Jack London and Downtown, crowded platforms, and a gridlock day �� traffic index 79, worst on I-880 South. My East Oakland stations, Fruitvale and Coliseum, both held at 0.83. That's not a coincidence I'm claiming; it's what the sheet says.

**Roads.** Every corridor improved against the prior cycle — I-880 North 100 to 89, I-880 South 98 to 92, I-980 100 to 86, Broadway 85 to 72, International 84 to 73. Heavy congestion remains, but the direction is right, and International Blvd — the corridor my neighbors actually walk and cross — moved from heavy to moderate. Event traffic from the Oaks home week is in the record on top of that.

**Infrastructure.** A medium-severity public-works spike in Glenview and a stalled bus in East Oakland. Neither on my docket, both on my radar, and neither acceptable to shrug at.

**Where the project stands.** Closure isn't decision. The schematics delivery and the documented Fruitvale community review are directed, and further design advancement waits on a public comment-and-response record that does not yet exist. Merchant covenants are executed and Mayer & Associates is under contract with community oversight provisions. Doña Esperanza's cart is in those drawings. I intend it to stay there when they're real.

That's my report. It's on the record as given.
